comparisons.peer_topic: Investment Management segment revenue sources and carried interest
comparisons.peer_summary: Investments revenues in the Investment Management segment are primarily from performance-based fees like carried interest, which are subject to reversal when certain funds exceed performance targets, as well as gains and losses from investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose the recognition of performance-based fees (incentive fees/carry) that are subject to reversal. GS recognizes incentive fees when it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur, which is generally when fees are no longer subject to market fluctuations, citing an unrecognized balance of $4.12 billion as of December 2024. Similarly, MS notes that within its Investment Management segment, revenues from carried interest (a performance-based fee) are subject to reversal, specifically when certain funds exceed performance targets.

sentences.text: These incentive fees are recognized when it is probable that a significant reversal of such fees will not occur.
Our estimated unrecognized incentive fees were $4.12 billion as of December 2024 and $3.77 billion as of December 2023.

These fees will be recognized, assuming no decline in fair value, if and when it is probable that a significant reversal of such fees will not occur, which is generally when such fees are no longer subject to fluctuations in the market value of the assets.

Within the Investment Management business segment, Investments revenues are primarily from performance-based fees in the form of carried interest, a portion of which is subject to reversal, and gains and losses from investments.
The business is entitled to receive carried interest when the return in certain funds exceeds specified performance targets.
